name: Ground heat from space
summary: How hot the ground and roofs are, seen day and night by NASA's Terra and Aqua satellites in 1 km pixels. It is the surface, not the air, and it needs a clear sky.

el.name: Θερμότητα εδάφους από το διάστημα
el.summary: Πόσο ζεστά είναι το έδαφος και οι στέγες, όπως τα βλέπουν μέρα και νύχτα οι δορυφόροι Terra και Aqua της NASA σε εικονοστοιχεία 1 km. Είναι η επιφάνεια, όχι ο αέρας, και θέλει καθαρό ουρανό.

publisher.name: NASA (MODIS land products, LP DAAC); subsets by ORNL DAAC

licence.attribution: NASA MODIS land products (LP DAAC), subset by ORNL DAAC TESViS, doi:10.3334/ORNLDAAC/1600

restrictions: ORNL DAAC asks users to cite both the subset tool (TESViS) and the product
The documentation we read gives no rate limit: we ask a few times a day, one call at a time

coverage.area: Global land (we read the four city centres)

update.note: One composite per 8-day period; it appears days after the period ends. We check twice a day.

variables.note: Day and night. Surface skin temperature, NOT air temperature.

quality.uncertainty: Each pixel carries its own error class (1, 2, 3 K or more); we use pixels up to 3 K. A mixed city pixel can be off by more.
known_issues: Surface temperature is not air temperature: a sunlit roof or road can be far hotter than the air at midday, and cooler at night
One value is an average over the clear days of 8; days with cloud are missing, so a cloudy week can leave no value
A pixel is about 1 km wide and mixes roofs, roads, trees and sometimes sea: it is an area, not a sensor at the school
Terra and Aqua are drifting off their orbits (Terra earlier, Aqua later) and NASA plans to retire both from late 2026 or early 2027
The satellites pass at set times only, so the value is not the daily maximum or minimum

upstream.name: NASA MODIS land surface temperature and emissivity, 8-day, 1 km (MOD11A2, MYD11A2), collection 6.1

use_for: Showing how much hotter or cooler the ground is than the air at day and at night
A reason to talk about shade, trees and cool roofs
not_for: Saying what the air temperature is, or comparing it with a thermometer as if it were the same
Saying a single street or school yard is hot or cool

notes: Built from the ORNL DAAC documentation (modis.ornl.gov/rst/api/v1: /dates and /subset, no key). It could not be tested against the live service from our build sandbox: the first check in production is the Railway log line from modis-lst and the Data layers card. Pair it with land-surface-heat (a Sentinel-3 candidate, not connected) and with modis-ndvi, which shows the greenness behind a cool or hot area.
